newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin names ex-Soviet marshal as aviation aide.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin names ex-Soviet marshal as aviation aide.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin named the last Soviet defence minister, Marshal Yevgeny Shaposhnikov, as an aide on Tuesday to oversee Russia's declining civil aviation and space sectors.
A presidential spokesman said a decree appointing Shaposhnikov, 55, did not specify whether he would have to leave his job as chairman of Russia's flagship international carrier Aeroflot.
But the spokesman suggested Shaposhnikov would not be able to combine the two posts.
"As a rule, presidential aides have to work day and night," the spokesman said. "They just cannot cope with any extra work."

Interfax news agency quoted a source in the presidential administration as saying Yeltsin was upset by the number of air accidents caused by the poor condition of planes owned by many companies formed after the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
The source said Shaposhnikov was chosen because Aeroflot, the former Soviet monopoly, had managed to keep itself technically up to scratch and commercially competitive.

Shaposhnikov became head of Aeroflot in 1995 after serving as commander in chief of the symbolic armed forces of the 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States formed on the ashes of the Soviet Union.
He also had spells as secretary of Yeltsin's policy-making Security council and as the president's watchdog at arms company Rosvooruzheniye.
